title: Cinderella and the Midnight Bells

story_parts.intro:
Once upon a time, in a sunny countryside of rolling hills, cypress trees, and silvery olive groves, there stood a rustic stone farmhouse with warm terracotta roof tiles. In that farmhouse lived a sweet girl named Cinderella, her Stepmother, and two Stepsisters. Cinderella's kind heart was as bright as the golden morning light, but her days were long and hard. From dawn until night, she swept the courtyard, tended the big hearth in the warm kitchen, and cooked simple bread and soup for everyone. At night, she slept by the fire, curled up with the friendly mice and a gentle dog who loved her dearly.

'Signora,' Cinderella would say politely each morning, 'may I help with anything else today?' But the Stepmother only frowned and gave her more chores, while her own daughters, the Stepsisters, twirled in their dresses covered with ribbons and lace. 'Look at her patched old dress!' they giggled. 'She belongs in the ashes, not at the table!' Yet Cinderella never answered with anything but kindness, for her heart was soft and full of love.

One bright day, bells rang out across the hills, and a town crier stood in the town piazza beside the fountain, calling out to all the neighbors who had gathered there. 'Hear ye, hear ye! The Prince shall hold a grand royal ball at the palazzo, and every young lady of the kingdom is invited!' The Stepsisters squealed with joy and rushed home to boast about their finest gowns. 'Mother, we shall dance with the Prince himself!'

Cinderella's eyes sparkled with hope. 'Signora, may I please come to the ball too?' But the Stepmother laughed a cold, unkind laugh. 'You? In that ragged dress? You would shame us all! You must stay home and scrub the floors.' The Stepsisters mocked her all the way to the carriage, and Cinderella watched them go, sitting alone on the marble step as the evening light turned gold over the hills. Still, she wiped her tears, hugged her little dog, and whispered, 'Perhaps someday things will be different.'
story_parts.developpement:
Just then, something wonderful happened. A soft light filled the garden, and there stood the Fairy Godmother, with a sparkling magic wand that glittered like the evening stars. 'Dear child,' she said with a warm smile, 'a heart as kind as yours deserves a night of joy. But remember this well: all my magic ends when the clock strikes midnight.'

With a wave of her wand, a bright orange pumpkin grew and grew until it became a shining carriage, and six gentle mice became fine horses to pull it. Cinderella's old patched dress melted away into a gown of shimmering azure, like the sky over the sea, and on her feet appeared delicate glass slippers that sparkled in the moonlight. 'Che meraviglia!' Cinderella gasped, twirling in wonder. 'Thank you, thank you!'

When Cinderella entered the grand palazzo, with its frescoed ballrooms, glittering chandeliers, and marble staircase, everyone fell silent with amazement. The Prince himself, whom all addressed as 'Sua Altezza,' bowed low and kissed her hand gently. 'May I have this dance?' he asked. And they danced to lively strings, twirling and laughing beneath the chandeliers, while the tables overflowed with regional sweets and cakes and festive treats. The Prince had never met anyone so kind and graceful, and he did not want the night to end.

But suddenly, Cinderella heard the first bell of midnight toll across the city. 'Oh no, I must go!' she cried, and she ran down the marble staircase as fast as she could. The Prince called after her, 'Wait! Please, tell me your name!' But Cinderella only hurried into her carriage, and as she ran, one glass slipper slipped off her foot and was left behind on the palace steps. When the last bell rang, the carriage became a pumpkin once more, the gown became patches, and only Cinderella's kind heart remained just as beautiful as before.
story_parts.conclusion:
The next morning, the Prince held the little glass slipper in his hands and made a promise. 'I will find the girl this slipper belongs to, and she shall be my bride.' He traveled through the countryside, past olive groves and cypress trees, from farmhouse to farmhouse, and the bells rang in every piazza as he came. When he reached the stone farmhouse, the Stepsisters pushed and shoved, trying desperately to squeeze their feet into the slipper. But it fit no one, for the glass slipper fits only its true owner.

'Is there no one else in this house?' asked the Prince. The Stepmother shook her head quickly, but the gentle dog barked and the little mice tugged at Cinderella's skirt, leading the Prince to the hearth kitchen where she stood in her simple patched dress. 'May I try?' Cinderella asked softly. She slipped her foot into the glass slipper, and it fit perfectly, sparkling in the morning sun. 'It is you!' the Prince cried joyfully. 'The one I danced with, the one with the kindest heart in all the kingdom!'

The Stepmother and the Stepsisters stood in shame, expecting Cinderella to be angry. But Cinderella smiled at them with forgiveness in her eyes. 'Do not be sad,' she said gently. 'I hope we can all be happy together someday.' And her loving heart melted their unkindness away. Cinderella and the Prince were married in the grand palazzo, and the bells rang for days across the hills. They lived happily ever after, proving that kindness, a loving heart, and forgiveness can overcome any hardship and lead to true happiness. The end.
